label: Game B
nuance_found: The core verb is catch a gust, carry it in the bell, release it into a mechanism. Chains of it (seed wheel, grille, windmill, pipe wheel) set up small spatial puzzles. One real wrinkle: a valve has to be turned so a pipe leads to the mill, and a gust spent on the wrong pipe drifts back. The Hollow guardian boss has the only real decision I found: its heart colour changes, the breath only turns the vane matching the current colour, and a wrong or late feed knocks the progress back (I got to 3/3 once and fell to 2/3). Mostly it is a fetch-and-deliver chain with one obvious next step, and the 'goto' assist did most of the walking, so I never had to plan a route.
audio: A procedural wind and drone ambience loop, soft chimes and chords on each gust catch and release, and a swirl whoosh. No real melodic music that I noticed.
furthest_progress: The Hollow guardian boss fight, vane feed 2/3 (reached 3/3 once, then lost progress). Before it: prologue, ring the morning bell, loft, Wake the three windmills 3/3 (Sails, Pipes, Ladders), sky bridge complete, two carvings in the gallery.
control_trouble: The camera clipped into the boss bell and a tree trunk, so I could not see where I was walking. Manual stick dodging in the boss fight was hard at 0.5 s sampling and I lost pips by standing still. The goto assist hung the whole harness once (carving) and sent me back down to the terrace once.
best_moment: The Hollow reveal of the giant guardian bell with the carved arms, and the painted village prologue.
worst_moment: Repeating the same catch, walk, release, deliver cycle for minutes, then the camera clipping into the boss so I could not read the fight.
verdict: It is a good-looking, atmospheric adventure with real direction behind it. The prologue art, the villagers and the guardian reveal feel like a small finished game. But the play is a fetch chain with a prompt button at every step, objective text that sometimes does not match what I am holding, and a camera that clips into things. The boss colour-matching vane puzzle is the first thing that makes me decide anything, and a wrong feed costs progress with little explanation. I would look at it again for the art, but I would not play it back-to-back with the other one.
